newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico PRI leads Sonora state governor race - poll.
newsitem.headline: Mexico PRI leads Sonora state governor race - poll.

text.p: The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) has a commanding lead in the July 6 election for governor of the northwestern state of Sonora, according to a poll published Friday by Reforma newspaper.
Reforma's poll showed PRI candidate Armando Lopez with 40 percent support, the same level as when the daily last polled in the state in February.

Lopez is a political ally of current Sonora governor Manlio Fabio Beltrones, a PRI hardliner who recently hit headlines after the New York Times accused him of links to drug traffickers -- an allegation he strongly denied.
The same poll showed Sonora voters gave Beltrones an approval rating of 68 percent, higher than the 65 percent they assigned to President Ernesto Zedillo.
The opposition National Action Party (PAN)'s candidate Enrique Salgado was in second place in the Sonora race with 24 percent, up from 22 percent in February, Reforma said.

In third place was Jesus Zambrano of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) with 12 percent. Twenty-one percent of voters had still not made up their minds how to vote or did not reply. Other candidates had three percent.
Reforma's poll was conducted between May 13-19 on a sample of 810 voters. It had a 3.5 percent margin of error.
Mexico votes on July 6 to elect a new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, the first-ever elected mayor of Mexico City and six state governors.

Reforma polls published last week put the PRI ahead to win the governorships of Queretaro and San Luis Potosi. Earlier polls suggest the PRI could win Campeche and Colima states and have predicted a close race between the PRI and the PAN in Nuevo Leon, the industrial state that includes Monterrey.
